title: Videos and Findings: every Reference reachable whether a publication files all, some or none under a section
description:
What: the Videos page (/videos/), the Findings page (/findings/, formerly /wire/) and each section's own lists (/<section>/videos/, and new /<section>/findings/) show every accepted Reference through one smooth infinite scroll, and look right whether a publication files all, some or none of its References under a section. Owner (Ryan, 2026-11-08): no heading of any kind on References that are not in a section ("not 'All videos', no category type heading"); at the top a few of the most recent, best References that are in no section; then a block per section (heading links to that section's own list, ends with "More <section> videos…"); then an infinite list of the remaining References that are in no section, again with no heading. A section's own list is an infinite list of all of its References. Findings gets the same design. Order everywhere: rolling seven-day buckets (newest first), then editor stars, then Cyclotron confidence, ties most recent; sections placed by their best item. No cap may hide an item.

Replaces the design shipped in MoM PR #141 (section groups only when sections exist, then a paged list headed "All videos" / "Not in a section yet").

Plan: Phase A ships site-only on the pinned engine (5.92.0): generator and template, hook, CSS, fixtures for every case, specs, browser checks, the Just Found page that takes over the pending References panel, release and cleanup. Phase B adopts two engine changes (Papyrus PPY-a9402d filters; PPY-2d9715 groups) and deletes the hook's HTML filtering and the one remaining cap. The design note is the first comment.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
DESIGN NOTE (architect, 2026-11-08). Implementers: follow this; the tasks under this epic carry the exact file changes.

1. PAGE ANATOMY

Terms. "Filed" = the Reference's `section` names a section this site has a page for (web/sections.json; the hook's `_section_resolver`). A Reference whose section has no page here (the fixtures' "Papyrus") counts as NOT filed: it is never given a group and appears in the lead and the stream with its section chip, so it stays reachable. "Lead" = the few best unfiled References at the top. "Stream" = the infinite list of the rest of the unfiled References. Neither has a heading; each has only an aria-label (lead: the page title, e.g. "Videos"; stream: "More videos" / "More findings"). The page's own title and lead sentence (page-top h1, "Videos" / "Videos we think are worth watching.") stay: they name the page, not a category.

/videos/ and /findings/, top to bottom:
  a. page-top (h1 + lead sentence + the site title card hanging in the last column at >= 900px).
  b. LEAD: the first 4 unfiled References in the site order, no heading. Rows: 4 = a feature row of 1 (picture beside words from 640px) + a row of 3. Fewer: 1 = [1], 2 = [2], 3 = [3]. None = no lead element at all.
  c. SECTION BLOCKS: one per filed section that has at least one item, placed by the position of its best item in the site order. Head: h2 with the section title linked to /<id>/videos/ (Findings: /<id>/findings/); no count. Cards in whole rows (existing `_reference_row_sizes`). Sizes: with a lead, ranks 0 and 1 show 6 (two rows of 3), rank 2 and later 3 (one row); without a lead (all filed), rank 0 shows 7 (feature + two rows of 3), ranks 1-2 show 6, later 3. Fewer items use `_row_sizes` (4 = 2+2, 5 = 3+2). Ends with "More <Title> videos…" ("More Privacy & Security findings…") linking to the section's list, only when the section has more items than the block shows.
  d. STREAM: one continuous grid, no heading. First page = 60 cards (the paged include asks for 64 and the hook lifts the first 4 into the lead), which is whole rows at every column count the site uses: 1 (<640), 2 (640-899), 3 (900-1511), 4 (1512-1839), 5 (1840-2199), 6 (>=2200). Later chunks (content-defined, 6-48 cards) append into the same grid, so only the very last row of the whole list can be partial. Load more + auto-load as the engine does (papyrus-reference-list.js).
  Blocks (b, c) use rows of 3 at >= 900px (2 + one spanning on tablet, 1 on phone) exactly as the current groups do; at >= 900 the first row of the first block (lead, else the rank-0 section) stops one column short of the site title card.

Three cases:
  - Nothing filed (MoM today: 132 videos, 684 findings, 0 filed): a, b (4), d (all the rest). No block. Nothing says "All videos".
  - Some filed: a, b (best 4 unfiled), c (blocks), d (rest of unfiled).
  - Everything filed (strict publications): a, c only. No lead, no stream, no Load more, no empty text. The first section gets the feature layout.

/<id>/videos/ and /<id>/findings/: a (title "<Title> videos" / "<Title> findings"; lead sentence "Every video filed under <Title>, this week's best first." / "Every source filed under <Title> that our editors and Cyclotron have accepted, this week's best first."), b (first 4 of the section), d (all the rest of the section). Same counts. The section front (/<id>/) links to its findings list with a new Findings panel under its Worth Watching videos: heading "Findings" linked to /<id>/findings/, one row of up to 3 findings (never videos), "More findings…" when there are more; no panel when the section has no finding. Its existing "More videos…" link to /<id>/videos/ stays.

Ordering: every include uses `select="recent" bucket="week"` (= the shared order inside rolling seven-day buckets, newest bucket first: stars, then Cyclotron confidence, unscored last, low stars last, ties newest arrival). Findings never show a video (owner: Findings lists accepted References that are not videos; today they include the 132 videos).

No repeats: the engine's paged list ignores what earlier components placed (docs/home-page.md "The shared order"), so the lead is NOT a second include. The hook moves the first 4 cards of the stream's first page into the lead. Lead and stream are then disjoint by construction, the chunk files are untouched, and no `skip` attribute is needed in the engine now or later. The section blocks' items are filed, the stream's are unfiled: disjoint.

Edge cases:
  - A section with no items: no block (and its own list page shows "No videos in <Title> yet." / "No findings in <Title> yet.").
  - Fewer unfiled than 4: the lead holds them all; the stream has nothing and is removed (no Load more).
  - Nothing accepted: no lead, no block; the stream's empty sentence shows ("No videos have been accepted yet." / "Nothing has been accepted yet.").
  - No sections declared (empty sections.json): every Reference is unfiled: lead + stream, no block.
  - A first stream page that is entirely filed: impossible in Phase B (the stream selects unfiled only). In Phase A the engine's list still holds filed items and the hook removes them, so a first page can come out empty while later chunks hold unfiled items; then the lead is short or empty and the script loads on (pace of 5 files, then "Press Load more"). Phase A removes the stream outright only when it can prove there is nothing unfiled (the group source include returned fewer than its count and none unfiled). MoM has 0 filed References today, so this does not occur on the live site before Phase B.

2. ENGINE vs HOOK

Gaps in Papyrus 5.92.0 (home_page_blocks.py): no "none of" section filter, no "not video" filter, no grouping of References by section, no skip; paged lists are the whole selection and do not consult the page ledger.
  - Option H (recommended, ships first, site-only, next MoM release, no engine release, no backend change beyond the normal site release): the hook filters tiles out of the stream and its chunk pages (filed ones on /videos/ and /findings/; videos on every findings list), lifts the lead, and builds the blocks from one whole-selection include with count="500". Costs: chunk files still hold filed items (wasted files and empty chunks in a heavily filed publication); the 500 count is a cap on which sections get a block (not on reachability: every item stays reachable at /<id>/videos/); the Markdown twins list up to 500 items, as today.
  - Option E (cleanup, Phase B): Papyrus PPY-a9402d adds `section="A|B"`, `notSection`, `notMedium` (applied to paged lists); PPY-2d9715 (existing story, spec added as a comment) adds `groups="section" per="7,6,6,3"` with `data-total`, uncapped. Cost: one Papyrus feat release, then a MoM version bump bundled into one MoM release (no new index, no schema change; other sites need not bump). It deletes the hook's tile filtering, the chunk filtering, the all-filed proof and the 500 cap; the lead lift stays.

3. ROLLOUT AND CLEANUP: see the release task MOM-d1534a. No bulk purge; the projector purges only what it rewrites; any manual invalidation is the exact list in that task (69 paths, so ask Ryan first). Old files: /wire/ and reference-lists/wire/ (2,148 objects on 2026-11-08) and the pending-list files under reference-lists/findings/recommended/ and reference-lists/videos/recommended/ are removed by a reviewed `--reconcile --dry-run --only <prefix>` then a reconcile; /wire/ gets a redirect to /findings/. The stream keeps list id `untagged` so its existing chunk files are reused, not orphaned.

4. OPEN QUESTION FOR RYAN (default taken): the pending panels ("Found by machines" on /findings/, "Not accepted yet" on /videos/) do not fit the new anatomy (they would sit under an infinite list, where nobody reaches them), and the home page's "Just Found" More link points at /findings/ for them. Default: move them to one new page, /just-found/ (all pending References, highest confidence first, infinite), point the home Just Found More link there, and drop both panels. Alternative if Ryan prefers: keep a pending panel above the section blocks.

Task order: MOM-d4782f generator -> MOM-949657 hook -> MOM-f0f559 CSS; MOM-cf309a fixtures; MOM-41c21a specs (after generator, hook, fixtures); MOM-193742 browser (after CSS, specs); MOM-94eacc Just Found (after generator); MOM-d1534a release and cleanup (after specs, browser, Just Found); MOM-d29573 Phase B (after the release and Papyrus PPY-a9402d + PPY-2d9715 released).
